title: Evaluation-normalized Hom comparison on locally closed generators
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\ge m\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$ with the quotient map [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules over constant coefficient rings on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ on a scheme $T$, and $H_R(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_R(U,V)$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The full subcategory $D^b_{ctf}$ consists of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval $[a,b]$: $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_R^L W)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $W$ and $i\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open, and $s=gj$. Set $Rs_{!,R}=g_{*,R}j_!$, $Rs_R^!=j^*Rg_R^!$ over $R=A,B$, using the etale closed-support adjunction [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, lem-exc-closed-ambient, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $L$ be a locally constant sheaf with finite projective $A$-module values on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$, in degree zero, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Put $N=Rs_A^!M$, $Q=H_A(L,N)$, and $L_B=F_SL$, $M_B=F_XM$. Let $q:F_XRs_{!,A}L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_{!,B}L_B$ be canonical open-extension/closed-direct-image scalar comparison; let $b:F_SN\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_B^!M_B$ be the exceptional comparison characterized by $\epsilon_{s,B}\circ Rs_{!,B}(b)\circ q_{s,N}=F_X\epsilon_{s,A}$. Let $c:F_XRs_{*,A}Q\to Rs_{*,B}F_SQ$ be the ordinary direct-image scalar comparison defined by the ordinary counit, and $u:F_SQ\to H_B(L_B,F_SN)$ the transpose of reduced evaluation. Write $I_R:Rs_{*,R}H_R(L_R,Rs_R^!M_R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(Rs_{!,R}L_R,M_R)$ for canonical internal adjunction, where $L_A=L$, $M_A=M$.

Then $N,Q$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible, all factors in the following derived-category composite are isomorphisms, and that composite equals the evaluation-transpose map $v_{Rs_{!,A}L,M}$:
$$F_XH_A(Rs_{!,A}L,M)\xrightarrow{F_XI_A^{-1}}F_XRs_{*,A}Q\xrightarrow{c}Rs_{*,B}F_SQ\xrightarrow{Rs_*u}Rs_{*,B}H_B(L_B,F_SN)\xrightarrow{Rs_*H_B(1,b)}Rs_{*,B}H_B(L_B,Rs_B^!M_B)\xrightarrow{I_B}H_B(Rs_{!,B}L_B,M_B)\xrightarrow{H_B(q,1)}H_B(F_XRs_{!,A}L,M_B).$$
Here the compact-support projection map in $I_R$ is the one formed from the open projection and closed proper projection maps. In particular it is this specified comparison, not merely some isomorphism between its endpoints, that is invertible for these locally closed generators.

proof.text: Apply etaleLocallyClosedShriekComparisons to M, obtaining N finite-Tor bounded constructible, the actual exceptional map b invertible and the pasted counit identity. The coefficient map and adjoint presentations agree definitionally.

Apply locallyProjectiveCoefficientHom on S to L and N. It gives L[0] and Q finite-Tor bounded constructible and invertibility of the specified evaluation transpose u. The support-comparison clause of the shriek theorem applied to L[0] makes q invertible.

Apply locallyClosedOrdinaryComparison_isIso to Q and its finite-Tor bounded constructibility. The new obligation contains exactly the finite-type geometric checks, direct-image theorem application and canonical compositor cancellation.

Apply locallyClosedInternalAdjunction_isIso over A and B to the specified internalAdjunction maps. Functors preserve these isomorphisms, their inverses and u,b,q. The intermediate lemma is the proper/open projection adjunction step and contains no coefficient comparison or constructibility assertion.

Set b=asIso of the actual exceptional coefficient map. The shriek theorem supplies exactly CounitCompatible, so apply internalAdjunction_pairing_change with M,L[0],N,Q. Precompose the equality with scalar extension of the inverse of I_A, cancel the inverse pair and expand functoriality of the direct image on u followed by Hom(1,b). This gives precisely the displayed composite equal to the evaluation transpose. Combine the invertibility assertions above.

The proof follows them: stratum Hom, then coefficient change through Rs_*, Rs^! and the finite-projective Hom, then transposition to v. The coefficient category is ordinary small-etale with the quotient map O_E/ϖ^n→O_E/ϖ^m, the same as the parent's. Step 1: X Noetherian (domain-calculus statement), then minimal condition ⇒ DCC ⇒ subsets quasi-compact; the (R/I)_h pieces give s of finite type, and the immersion diagonal is an iso, so s is separated. Step 2: dim S ≤ dim X because closures keep chains strict; the hypotheses of lem-coef-etale-lisse-hom-reduction match verbatim and give N and Q in D^b_ctf, L Tor [0,0], u iso. Step 3: L is lisse with finite stalks, hence constructible. The shriek node's q_s = g_*(q_j)∘c_g is the item's q. The counit identity determines b uniquely (adjunction bijection, q_{s,N} invertible), so it is the item's b. Step 4: B is a cyclic A-module, s is separated of finite type, Q is ctf, and the counit-defined c matches. Step 5: pairing-change hypotheses hold. I_A and I_B are presupposed isomorphisms both in that node and in the item's own notation. Functors preserve isomorphisms. Step 6: precomposing D = v∘F_X I_A with F_X I_A^{-1} gives the seven-arrow word; marking it elementary is correct. Edge cases checked: n=m, m=1, rank 0, empty X or S, j=id, g=id. The lem-per-ctf-hom-* nodes are F_ℓ / dualizing-hypothesis variants, not duplicates. Accepted tool uses: Noetherian-topology x2 and the finite-type dimension lemma, generic and used only to check hypotheses. No SGA citation.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedComparison
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (n m : ℕ+) (hmn : m ≤ n)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))]
    {S Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion g]
    (j : S ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (L : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat (coefficient l E n)))
    (_hL : ∃ d : Scheme.LocallyConstantDatum L, ∀ i : d.cover.I₀,
      ∃ P : ModuleCat (coefficient l E n),
        Module.Finite (coefficient l E n) P ∧ Module.Projective (coefficient l E n) P ∧
        Nonempty (L.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i) ≅
          (constantSheaf (S.smallEtaleTopology.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i))
            (ModuleCat (coefficient l E n))).obj P))
    (M : DerivedCategoryModule (coefficient l E n) X)
    (_hM : WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E n n.property X M) :
    WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E n n.property S
      (exceptionalObject g j M) ∧
    WeilConjectures.finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E n n.property S
      (innerHom g j ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L) M) ∧
    IsNormalizedComparison (reduction l E n m hmn) g j
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L) M
